filename: Data-driven parameterization development using ARM observations and models.pdf
title: Breakout Session Report: Data-driven parameterization development using ARM observations and models
venue: DOE Atmospheric Radiation Measurement (ARM) / Atmospheric System Research (ASR) PI Meeting
parameterization_target: Multiple processes: cloud microphysics, warm rain process rates, turbulence/near-surface momentum and energy exchange, 3D radiative transfer, aerosol processes
testbed_rationale: This document is a community breakout session summary report highlighting research directions, presentations, and challenges, rather than presenting or releasing a specific benchmark dataset.
pain_points: Need for physical insight and domain knowledge in machine architectures rather than trial-and-error approaches
Long timelines (often several years) required for cross-disciplinary collaboration between atmospheric scientists and machine learning researchers
High computational cost of sampling methods (e.g., MCMC needing millions of samples for high-dimensional models), necessitating fast surrogate models
Interpretability challenges with equation discovery and symbolic regression (e.g., understanding equations discovered by AI Feynman)
Handling multiscale interactions in causal discovery when processes span minutes to days; mismatch between observation time resolution and process timescales can lead to erroneous causal attribution
Lack of standardized community tools and software infrastructure to implement ML parameterizations directly inside host climate models
Exploration vs. exploitation tradeoff between pursuing cutting-edge scientific ML methods and implementing near-term operational parameterizations in Earth system models
extraction_notes: Breakout session report from the August 8, 2023 DOE ARM/ASR meeting. Specific individual presentations discussed tools (e.g., PART-MC, AI Feynman, EAGLES project), but no individual standalone datasets were detailed with accessibility info.
